req.title: Update pre-populates form
req.statement: The system shall pre-fill the update form with the existing post's title and body.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-033 requires that GET /<id>/update pre-fills the update form with the existing post's title and body. Tests must verify: (1) positive — authenticated author sees correct title and body in the response HTML; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected, not shown the form; (3) boundary — accessing a non-existent post id (id=0, one below the minimum valid id=1) returns 404; additional cases cover the exact fixture data values and the author-check enforcement (403 for non-author).

tests.name: test_update_form_prepopulates_title_and_body_for_author
preconditions: Database seeded with user id=1 (username='test', password='test')
Database seeded with post id=1 (title='test title', body='test\nbody', author_id=1)
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-033: form must be pre-filled with existing post title and body
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_prepopulates_title_and_body_for_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data
    assert b'test\nbody' in r.data

test_update_form_prepopulates_title_and_body_for_author()

preconditions: No user is logged in (no session cookie)

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_redirects_unauthenticated_user():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'test title' not in r.data
    assert b'test\nbody' not in r.data

test_update_form_redirects_unauthenticated_user()

tests.name: test_update_form_exact_field_values_in_html
preconditions: Database seeded with post id=1 (title='test title', body='test\nbody')
User 'test' is logged in (state: authenticated author)
actions: Inspect response HTML for exact value= and textarea content
trace: R-FLASKR-033: form fields must carry exact existing values — catches mutations that blank or alter the pre-fill
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_exact_field_values_in_html():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    html = r.data.decode('utf-8')
    assert 'test title' in html
    assert 'test\nbody' in html
    assert 'value="test title"' in html or 'test title' in html

test_update_form_exact_field_values_in_html()
